## What is still open
- PR #247 fixes the Orbitly/iOS event loss but isn't merged: CI must go green and Maya must approve. She wants the Orbitly drop count for Thursday's call — about **1.18M legitimate events (8.1% of iOS volume)** [1][2]
- Once #247 is merged and deployed, replay Orbitly (`prj_0rb1`) and Zest (`prj_z3st`) from landing for 13/11 onward (~40 min for Orbitly), then confirm the dedupe counter stays near zero [1][2]
- Add an ingest dead-letter queue alert above 1,000 messages before Friday's incident review on 20/11 [7]
- The note asking the iOS team to restore UUID `event_id`s in kestrel-ios 3.2.1 is drafted but still needs to go out [1]

## What changed
- Zest's dashboards are complete again after the backfill, and their Zendesk ticket is closed [6]
- The 12/11 postmortem is final; Noa presents it at Friday's incident review [3][7]
- CI and Dockerfile moved to Go 1.23.4 (#245, merged) [4]

## What you did
- Traced the ~8% Orbitly iOS funnel drop to the dedupe introduced by #240 keying on `event_id`, while kestrel-ios 3.2.0 sends per-session counters instead of the UUIDs the ingest contract requires. You re-keyed dedupe on project/device/event, kept replay protection, added tests, and opened #247 with Maya as reviewer [1]
- Scoped the blast radius: Orbitly accounts for 99% of drops, Zest is marginally hit on a pilot store app (3,812 events, 0.4% of its traffic); all other projects are unaffected [1]
